text: Conventional pond aquaculture uses relatively enclosed water bodies, making effluent prone to eutrophication and potentially affecting surrounding waters after discharge. To improve effluent treatment and overall benefits, Tianjin introduced a pond enclosure recirculating aquaculture system and conducted trials to rear large-sized largemouth bass fingerlings in that system, obtaining promising demonstration results. This article summarizes the construction of the pond enclosure system and its application to largemouth bass fingerling rearing, with the aim of providing a reference for further adoption in northern China and supporting the green transformation and upgrading of aquaculture.

As intensive aquaculture continues to expand, high-density culture can reduce the growth performance of aquatic animals, increase disease outbreaks, and contribute to antibiotic misuse, undermining sustainable development. As unicellular fungi, yeasts possess cell wall components and metabolites with immunostimulatory and probiotic functions. They offer advantages in improving growth performance, disease resistance, and feed utilization in aquatic animals and have become important microbial resources in aquaculture. This review discusses the biological properties, nutritional characteristics, functions, mechanisms of action, and specific applications of yeast in aquaculture, providing a theoretical reference for healthy and sustainable industry development.

To improve the stability and modeling of temporal dependencies in dissolved oxygen prediction for aquaculture, this study proposes a bidirectional long short-term memory neural network (BiLSTM*) incorporating self-attention. The attention mechanism dynamically adjusts weights across time points to identify important temporal features, while the BiLSTM* models complex interactions between dissolved oxygen and other water-quality indicators. The architecture combines self-attention, model structure, and optimization components to improve long-sequence processing and dependency capture. After preliminary experiments in a tank and a natural lake using an underwater robotic water-quality monitoring platform, the model was evaluated on an offshore aquaculture platform. The proposed model achieved a mean absolute error of 6.2 × 10^-3 and a root mean square error of 9.49 × 10^-3. Compared with LSTM and BiLSTM* models, it showed improved accuracy and generalization for long-horizon prediction.

China has the world's largest freshwater aquaculture production, yet participation in aquaculture insurance has developed slowly. The diversity of cultured species and farming systems, complex culture environments, disease-control challenges, substantial market-price fluctuations, and asymmetric risk information can increase moral hazard and adverse selection in the insurance market. Drawing on prospect theory and cognitive behavioral theory, this study used 2024 survey data from aquaculture operators in the national specialized freshwater fish industry technology system. A Probit model was applied to test the effects of risk perception and attitudes toward purchasing insurance on participation, and Bootstrap mediation analysis examined the mechanism through which attitudes influence decisions. Both risk perception and attitudes toward insurance were positively associated with insurance participation, although effects differed across risk categories. Attitudes toward insurance were the stronger determinant of participation, and partially mediated the relationship between risk perception and participation, accounting for 75% of the indirect pathway as reported in the study. The type of business operator moderated this mediated pathway. These findings provide suggestions for improving aquaculture insurance participation and supporting the development of freshwater aquaculture.

The spread of antibiotic resistance in nearshore aquaculture environments poses major risks to environmental quality, public health, and food safety, and challenges the prevention and treatment of human infections. Viruses can facilitate the spread of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in aquatic environments through horizontal gene transfer. However, knowledge of ARG contamination associated with the virome in nearshore aquaculture environments remains limited. This review summarizes the distribution of virome-associated ARGs and the main mechanisms of virus-mediated horizontal ARG transfer, analyzes environmental factors affecting their dissemination, reviews recent progress, and identifies unresolved scientific questions. It aims to improve understanding of the ecological role of viruses in ARG transmission in marine aquaculture and to inform measures for reducing antibiotic resistance and managing ARG pollution.

To assess bacterial resistance and resistance-gene transmission under monoculture and mixed poultry–fish freshwater bass farming, sediment, water, fish, and chicken manure were sampled from the two systems. A total of 243 bacterial isolates were identified, and their resistance and transmission characteristics were compared using Kirby–Bauer susceptibility tests, PCR detection of resistance genes and integrons, and conjugation experiments under antibiotic pressure. In the poultry–fish system, resistance rates to 11 antibiotics were significantly higher than in monoculture; chicken manure showed the most severe resistance, and multidrug-resistant isolates were more prevalent. Seventeen resistance genes were detected in the mixed system versus 15 in monoculture, with 11 genes showing significantly higher detection rates. All three integron classes were detected more frequently in the mixed system, and co-occurrence networks linked integrons to quinolone and sulfonamide resistance genes. Conjugation experiments showed a higher transfer frequency of sul1 in the mixed system; subinhibitory concentrations of sulfamonomethoxine further increased conjugation frequency. Overall, mixed poultry–fish farming intensified the enrichment and spread of resistance genes, indicating a need for stronger oversight to reduce dissemination risks.

Bioremediation technologies have been applied to the restoration and enhancement of microbial communities in aquatic environments. By strengthening the self-purification capacity of water bodies, these approaches can improve environmental quality. Drawing on practical cases and associated technical data, this article examines the effects and implementation of bioremediation techniques in polluted marine aquaculture waters, with the aim of supporting the healthy and environmentally sustainable development of marine aquaculture.

This review examines the development and future trends of aquavoltaic systems in China and internationally and assesses their potential to address climate change, improve energy structures, and increase aquaculture efficiency. Through a review and synthesis of the literature, it describes system configurations, their suitability for aquatic environments, and their interactions with aquaculture operations. Aquavoltaics can make dual use of space for power generation and aquaculture while potentially reducing water evaporation, cooling photovoltaic modules, and conserving land. However, uncertainties remain concerning environmental impacts, the durability of photovoltaic components, and coordination with fisheries activities. Future work should strengthen fundamental research, optimize site selection and system layouts, emphasize ecological protection and professional management, and improve relevant policies and standards to support sustainable aquavoltaic development.

The complex environment and frequent water-quality fluctuations of saline–alkaline aquaculture pose challenges for farm management. A multisensor data acquisition system can monitor key parameters in real time, including dissolved oxygen, pH, temperature, oxidation–reduction potential (ORP), and total dissolved solids (TDS). The proposed system uses an STM32 microcontroller together with a high-precision analog-to-digital converter (ADC) for data collection and employs direct memory access (DMA) to improve transmission efficiency. These features can enhance monitoring accuracy, support intelligent farm management, and contribute to the sustainability of aquaculture on saline–alkaline land.

Chinese herbal feed additives are prepared from traditional herbal materials and may be classified by physical form, processing method, and formula composition. Common ingredients include Astragalus, Epimedium, Isatis root, and hawthorn. In addition to their perceived natural and safe characteristics, such additives can enhance immunity, improve production performance and animal-product quality, and support reproduction. Their use in livestock, poultry, and aquaculture may contribute to disease prevention, animal health, productivity, and product quality. Although wider application still faces challenges, Chinese herbal feed additives offer a possible direction for more efficient, safer, and environmentally sustainable animal production.

Rapid growth in global aquaculture has intensified phosphorus pollution in discharged effluent. Existing removal approaches face efficiency and cost limitations that hinder the industry's transition to greener production. Considering the physicochemical characteristics of aquaculture effluent, this review assesses modification strategies and phosphorus adsorption mechanisms for four classes of materials: solid-waste-derived adsorbents, carbon nanomaterials, layered double hydroxides (LDHs), and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). It examines the combined roles of surface complexation, ion exchange, and electrostatic adsorption under complex water-quality conditions, as well as methods to enhance adsorption capacity and regeneration through material modification and structural control. Integrated processes, including adsorption combined with membrane separation and biologically enhanced regeneration, are proposed and discussed using application cases in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS). Future priorities include adsorbent stability under variable hydraulic conditions and life-cycle environmental assessment, with the aim of promoting closed-loop phosphorus management in low-carbon aquaculture engineering.

With the rapid development of aquaculture, microbially fermented feeds are being used more widely. Microbial fermentation can transform antinutritional factors in conventional plant protein ingredients, improving feed utilization while supporting animal health and immune function. This article first analyzes key technical considerations in producing microbially fermented feed and then examines specific aquaculture applications using Pacific white shrimp as an example.

To address highly repetitive tasks and long sampling periods in aquaculture water-quality monitoring, an unmanned surface vessel integrating water sampling and autonomous navigation was designed using an integrated navigation system. Experimental verification showed high navigation and positioning accuracy: deviations at monitoring locations were within 0.02 m, with an average deviation of 0.015 m. Its monitoring and sampling functions operated stably, transmitting water temperature, turbidity, and other measurements in real time, and collecting water samples accurately at a depth of 50 cm. The system provides a potentially economical and reliable solution for comprehensive aquaculture water-quality monitoring.

Algae and their derivatives exhibit functional characteristics resembling certain applications of antibiotics in animal production. They may help prevent or alleviate diseases in farmed animals and promote growth. Existing research indicates that algae and their derivatives can act as natural prebiotics, modifying the structure and composition of the intestinal microbiota across various farmed species. By promoting beneficial microorganisms and suppressing the abundance of pathogens, they may improve animal health and growth performance. These properties suggest innovative alternatives to antibiotic use in sustainable aquaculture, poultry production, and livestock farming, with the potential to support greener, more efficient, and more sustainable production systems.

Fishmeal is traditionally a high-quality protein ingredient in aquafeeds, but limited resources, high prices, and unstable supply have become major obstacles to sustainable aquaculture. Identifying economical and sustainable protein alternatives is therefore a major research focus. Plant protein sources are considered promising fishmeal substitutes because they are widely available, have relatively stable production, and are generally less expensive. This review summarizes the types and characteristics of plant protein ingredients and progress in their use as fishmeal replacements in feeds for aquatic animals. It also discusses challenges encountered in practical production and potential improvements in their application, providing a reference for the development and use of alternative proteins in aquafeeds.

A simple, portable nitrite detector based on an ESP32-C3 Internet-of-Things chip was designed and constructed to monitor nitrite levels in aquaculture water promptly. The device is low-cost, compact, and easy to use. A single ESP32-C3 microcontroller performs signal acquisition, analog-to-digital conversion, data processing, display, and transmission; Bluetooth enables wireless connections to mobile phones and other terminals for remote communication and process control. Repeated measurements of nitrite-containing water samples were close to those obtained with a commercial spectrophotometer, indicating good accuracy and stability.

Camellia oleifera fruit husks were extracted by acid hydrolysis, and extract components were identified by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). In vitro assays evaluated antibacterial activity against five common aquatic pathogens, while a culture experiment assessed effects on the growth, antioxidant capacity, and immunity of juvenile largemouth bass. The extract contained esters (15.42%), furans (61.75%), phenols (8.43%), and ketones (3.90%). It exhibited marked antibacterial activity against Vibrio harveyi, Pseudomonas plecoglossicida, Edwardsiella tarda, Aeromonas hydrophila, and Vibrio alginolyticus, with high sensitivity reported for the tested bacteria. During a 56-day culture trial, adding 0.1% fruit-husk extract to the feed (diet A1) promoted juvenile growth (weight gain rate 441.19% ± 9.49%) and feed utilization (feed conversion ratio 1.00 ± 0.01). Antioxidant and immune indices also improved, including increased serum total superoxide dismutase activity, total antioxidant capacity, alkaline phosphatase activity, and immunoglobulin M, together with decreased malondialdehyde.

Using numerical simulation and engineering experience, a two-dimensional horizontal model was applied to analyze aquaculture-effluent discharge in Dajiao Bay, Hainan. Environmental carrying capacity, economic considerations, and discharge requirements were jointly assessed to select an outfall location. The preferred location was designated D9. A discharge standard more stringent than the Class I limits in Table 2 of the Hainan Aquaculture Effluent Discharge Standard (DB46/475-2023) was proposed: suspended solids no greater than 22 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand no greater than 4.5 mg/L, inorganic nitrogen no greater than 1.6 mg/L, and reactive phosphate no greater than 0.22 mg/L. The maximum proposed flow was 200,000 m³/day, intended to meet the aquaculture park's near-term discharge demand over five years. A longer-term outfall location for a ten-year horizon was also identified. The study provides a technical reference for outfall planning and sustainable development of coastal aquaculture.

Aquaculture effluent has become an important factor affecting improvements in watershed water quality. To assess ecological treatment performance and improve water quality around farming areas, a demonstration project based on ecological treatment was implemented. After implementation, the permanganate index and total nitrogen decreased significantly, with removal rates of 50.80% and 58.21%, respectively. The combined water-treatment and operation-and-maintenance cost was approximately CNY 0.15–0.20 per cubic meter, indicating favorable economics. The project and its findings provide a reference for managing aquaculture effluent.

Freshwater fish are an important component of aquatic biodiversity and play significant ecological roles. Their gut microbiota consist of microorganisms living symbiotically in the intestinal tract and are involved in host nutrient metabolism and health. Microbial diversity is closely associated with host health. This review discusses the composition and importance of freshwater fish gut microbiota; their roles in digestion and absorption, growth and development, and immune regulation; and the potential of gut-associated probiotics to improve nutrition, immunity, water quality, and stress tolerance. It also highlights opportunities to screen probiotics and develop microbial biomarkers, providing a reference for using gut microbial resources in freshwater fish disease control and sustainable aquaculture.

As aquaculture becomes increasingly intensive and large-scale, production benefits have risen, but diseases of farmed aquatic animals have also become more frequent. Safe, effective, and environmentally friendly feed additives are therefore needed. Microecological preparations offer potential benefits in water purification and promotion of aquatic animal growth, with ecological and economic advantages that are compatible with sustainable development and environmental protection. This review discusses the classification, mechanisms of action, and research progress of microecological preparations. It aims to provide a reference for their further use as water-quality improvers and feed additives in aquaculture.

The red-eye fish, a cyprinid known for a red spot above its eye, occurs in waters across northern and southern China. It grows quickly, adapts well to different conditions, has an omnivorous diet, and offers relatively low culture costs and high market prices. As a species native to the Yellow River, it also has favorable prospects for distinctive aquaculture in Shanxi Province, where the river extends 966 km across multiple cities and counties. This study conducted a standardized pond culture trial and comprehensively examined fingerling size, stocking density, feed, disease prevention, and related management practices to inform the standardized pond production of this species.

As aquaculture expands, high-density intensive systems can degrade culture environments, reduce animal immunity, and increase disease incidence, thereby constraining industry development. Conventional chemical treatments and antibiotics may promote resistance and pose ecological and food-safety risks. Traditional Chinese medicines are widely available, are considered less prone to resistance development, and may have relatively low adverse effects. They can enhance immune function and disease resistance in aquatic animals. In light of recent advances in the modernization of traditional Chinese medicine, this review examines the effects of single medicinal herbs, compound herbal preparations, and herbal extracts on immune responses, antioxidant capacity, and disease resistance in aquatic animals, providing a theoretical basis for aquaculture applications.

As demand for aquatic products increases, aquaculture production continues to expand, and intelligent feeding technologies can help reduce costs and improve farming efficiency. To identify research trends, hotspots, and future directions, this study analyzed literature published between 2015 and 2024, including 310 Chinese-language papers from CNKI and 64 English-language papers from Web of Science. CiteSpace and VOSviewer were used to examine publication output, major authors, institutions, and keywords. Publication activity increased steadily during the study period, with China accounting for the largest output. Shanghai Ocean University and Auburn University were identified as major institutions, and Zhao Dean and Tian Changfeng as prominent researchers. Trends included increasingly intelligent, precise, and unmanned aquaculture systems. Research hotspots involved machine vision, deep learning, the Internet of Things, and refined decision systems. Largemouth bass, shrimp and crabs, and rainbow trout were frequently studied; cage culture and industrial recirculating aquaculture were major application settings. Future directions include combining emerging technologies, extending systems to additional cultured species, and integrating renewable energy.

Animal farming plays an important role in Chinese agriculture and has grown rapidly, contributing substantially to economic growth and farmers' incomes. However, this expansion has also caused serious environmental pollution through the discharge of large quantities of wastewater, waste gas, and solid waste. China has undertaken many years of research and practical work on pollution-control technologies for animal farming and has achieved some results. This article reviews their development and current status, analyzes challenges facing existing technologies, and proposes recommendations for researchers and practitioners.

Antibiotics are widely used in aquaculture to prevent and treat diseases, contributing to the emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in culture waters. ARGs are now widespread in aquaculture ecosystems and can be discharged into the environment with effluent, threatening ecosystem integrity and human health. Reliable ARG detection and removal technologies are therefore important. This review discusses detection methods, including conventional microbial culture, PCR, DNA hybridization, microarrays, and metagenomics, as well as commonly used approaches to remove ARGs from water. It aims to provide a theoretical basis for rapid detection and effective removal of resistance genes in aquaculture systems.

Siyang County in northern Jiangsu is a major aquaculture area, with nearly 18,000 hectares of aquaculture, including 10,000 hectares devoted to Chinese mitten crabs, more than half the county's total. Frequent disease outbreaks in recent years have seriously constrained crab farming. From 2020 to 2022, the county aquatic animal disease prevention and control center monitored bacterial diseases in crab farms. The work was intended to provide baseline data for disease control and epidemiological research and to guide farmers in selecting and using medicines appropriately and implementing ecologically oriented disease prevention.

An investigation of antibiotics and antibiotic resistance genes was conducted in East Taihu Lake after removal of net enclosures and in the aquaculture area of Yangcheng Lake to evaluate the environmental consequences of enclosure removal. Antibiotic concentrations in East Taihu were significantly lower after removal than in aquaculture zones, ranging from 0 to 9.70 ng/L at four sampling sites, versus 53.14 ng/L in a fishpond. Concentrations were also low in Yangcheng Lake aquaculture waters (0–0.04 ng/L). However, resistance-gene concentrations in East Taihu were similar to those in Yangcheng Lake aquaculture areas. At East Taihu site 1, ribosomal protection genes were the predominant resistance genes; antibiotic inactivation genes dominated at East Taihu sites 4, 7, and 9, in crab and fish ponds, and in the central-southern and southwestern areas of Yangcheng Lake. Antibiotic efflux genes predominated in southeastern Yangcheng Lake.

Increasing intensification of aquaculture has been accompanied by more frequent diseases, particularly bacterial infections. Prevention and treatment have depended heavily on antibiotics, while the emergence of multidrug-resistant bacteria and the slow development of new antibiotics make alternative therapies increasingly important. Bacteriophages are promising alternatives because of their relatively specific host ranges, limited ecological effects, and abundance in natural environments. This review summarizes progress in phage therapy against common aquaculture pathogens, including Aeromonas hydrophila, Vibrio harveyi, Vibrio parahaemolyticus, and Aeromonas salmonicida. It describes relevant phage characteristics, treatment outcomes, and conditions for effective application. The review compares the advantages of phage therapy with other antimicrobial approaches, discusses potential limitations, and considers future prospects for phage-based disease control in aquaculture.

To address low efficiency, delayed responses, and limited precision in conventional aquaculture water-quality management, this study designed an Internet-of-Things-based multiparameter monitoring system. Built around an STM32 microcontroller, the system integrates high-precision sensors, LoRa long-range communication, and a cloud platform to collect and transmit dissolved oxygen, temperature, pH, turbidity, and other key water-quality indicators in real time. It also supports remote control of aerators and pumps to establish a closed-loop regulation process. The software uses Alibaba Cloud's IoT platform for remote monitoring and automatic control. Practical tests reported mean relative errors below 3% for water-temperature, pH, and dissolved-oxygen measurements and a 100% response success rate for remote-control commands. The results indicate that the system can provide accurate and reliable support for intelligent aquaculture management.

Black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens) larvae are rich in fat, protein, and minerals and have high nutritional value, rapid growth, and relatively simple rearing requirements. As an emerging high-quality feed protein source, they may partially replace soybean meal and fishmeal in animal diets. Appropriate replacement levels can improve growth performance, antioxidant status, disease resistance, and egg and meat quality. This review covers the biological characteristics and principal nutrients of black soldier fly and recent applications of black soldier fly ingredients as substitutes for conventional protein sources in aquaculture, poultry, and pig production, providing a reference for their wider use in animal farming.

The effects of potassium and magnesium supplementation using slow-release potassium magnesium sulfate were investigated in freshwater-reared Pacific white shrimp. A total of 90,000 healthy shrimp, with an initial body weight of 0.0017 ± 0.0001 g and length of 1.267 ± 0.008 cm, were randomly assigned to five groups. The control received conventional shrimp feed; three treatments received feed containing 2, 4, or 6 kg/t of slow-release potassium magnesium sulfate; and a positive control received 2 kg/t of a magnesium sulfate–calcium chloride mixture. Each treatment had six replicates, with 3,000 shrimp stocked per 2 m × 3 m × 1.5 m pond. Fifty shrimp were sampled from each pond at the start and on days 35 and 70 for body weight and length measurements. Recovered shrimp were counted at the end of the trial, and muscle texture was measured in five randomly selected shrimp from each pond. Slow-release potassium magnesium sulfate significantly increased weight gain and weight gain rate, reduced the feed conversion ratio, improved survival, and enhanced muscle texture. Its effects were broadly comparable to those of the magnesium sulfate–calcium chloride mixture. Under these conditions, dietary supplementation at 4 kg/t was beneficial for shrimp growth, survival, and muscle texture.

This article briefly reviews the biological characteristics and nutritional value of black soldier fly, as well as research on its use as a fishmeal substitute, the extraction of antimicrobial peptides, and the conversion of cyanobacterial sludge. Black soldier fly has high reproductive capacity, low rearing costs, and is described as non-toxic and non-polluting. It contains abundant protein, diverse amino acids, and vitamins, trace elements, and fatty acids required by animals, making it a promising new insect-derived protein source. Black soldier fly farming is an emerging sector, and its products may be particularly suitable as feed protein ingredients for aquaculture.

Integrated fish–rice culture combines crop production and aquaculture as a potentially environmentally friendly approach to improving overall pond productivity. To investigate a sustainable and efficient pond-culture model, a trial was conducted on the southern slopes of the Qinling Mountains in 2022. After four months of combined fish culture and rice cultivation, the integrated system was compared with a control pond. Reported results showed an 11.4% increase in fish yield, a 31.0% reduction in fish disease incidence, and a 19.2% improvement in overall economic returns. Water quality also improved: ammonia nitrogen and nitrite levels in the experimental pond were significantly lower than in the control pond (P < 0.05). The findings suggest that integrated fish–rice culture can support fish and crop production while contributing to ecological effluent management and more efficient aquaculture.

Bile acids (BAs) are amphipathic sterol compounds classified by origin as primary or secondary bile acids. Primary bile acids are synthesized from cholesterol in the liver and enter the intestine, where gut microbes in the distal ileum and proximal colon convert some of them to secondary bile acids. Most intestinal bile acids return to the liver through enterohepatic circulation, while the remainder are excreted in feces. Studies indicate that bile acids contribute to carbohydrate and lipid homeostasis, immune function, and gut microbial community structure in fish. However, bile acid composition varies among fish species, and the benefits of particular bile acids can differ across species. Current knowledge of bile acid composition, classification, and functions in fish remains limited. This review summarizes bile acid types, main receptors, biological functions, and research progress in fish, identifies outstanding problems, and provides a reference for future research and effective aquaculture applications.

Based on representative examples, this article introduces nine ecological and healthy aquaculture models and their practical applications: engineered pond recirculating systems, integrated rice–fish farming, deep-water storm-resistant cages, ecological culture and stock enhancement in large water bodies, industrial recirculating aquaculture, green aquaculture in saline–alkaline waters, aquaponics, integrated multitrophic aquaculture, and container-based recirculating systems. Developing ecologically healthy fisheries is considered important for increasing the productive potential of fishery ecosystems, stabilizing and supporting fishery economies, and accelerating the practical application of scientific and technological advances in modern intensive aquaculture.

China is a major aquaculture producer, and marine shellfish account for the largest share of its marine aquaculture output; China has ranked first globally in this sector for many years. The shellfish industry has made notable progress toward greener and healthier development amid rapid advances in technologies, industries, and business models. Nevertheless, substantial differences among coastal aquaculture environments, shellfish biology, and farming systems pose challenges for breeding improved varieties, producing and supplying large-sized seed, upgrading mechanization and intelligent equipment, and integrating the full value chain. These challenges hinder green development. This article proposes measures involving policy support, technological innovation, and industry integration to promote the healthy development of China's marine shellfish industry.

Unmanned smart aquaculture factories offer a potential solution to the dependence of conventional aquaculture on manual experience and extensive management. By integrating digital and intelligent technologies throughout production, these systems aim to implement unmanned operations through a closed-loop architecture connecting biological-state monitoring, environmental regulation, resource management, production decisions, data acquisition, and execution feedback. This review describes the operating mechanisms and research status of such systems. It examines intelligent precision feeding, water-quality monitoring and analysis, disease prevention and early warning, growth modeling, intelligent equipment, and automated processing, including their implementation approaches, core algorithms, and application bottlenecks. Although a range of technologies is now available, challenges remain in fusing heterogeneous data from complex aquatic environments and in generalizing models under high-density culture conditions. Future research should emphasize hybrid modeling that combines biological mechanisms with data-driven approaches, cloud-edge collaborative inference, and interdisciplinary innovation to advance sustainable intelligent aquaculture factories.

Objective: To systematically describe the distribution and ecological risks of non-native fish in natural waters of the Yangtze River Basin. Methods: Survey data from 65 sites collected during the 2017–2021 Yangtze Fisheries Resources and Environment Survey were combined with a literature review to examine non-native fish diversity and distribution. Risk levels were assessed using the Aquatic Species Invasiveness Screening Kit (AS-ISK). Results: Thirty-eight non-native fish species were recorded, representing eight orders, 15 families, and 29 genera: 17 cypriniforms, seven siluriforms, five perciforms, four acipenseriforms, two characiforms, and one species each in Cyprinodontiformes, Osmeriformes, and Lepisosteiformes. Most originated in Asia (17 species), and 20 were introduced primarily for aquaculture. Non-native fish were recorded across the surveyed river systems and lakes except the Tuotuo River and Hengjiang River; the Three Gorges Reservoir area had the most species (22). AS-ISK classified 19, six, and 13 species as high, medium, and low risk, respectively. The five highest-risk species were mosquitofish, suckermouth catfish, Nile tilapia, largemouth bass, and Mozambique tilapia. Conclusion: The basin contains numerous non-native fish with complex distributions. Although severe ecological damage has not yet been documented, potential risks remain high. These findings may inform prevention and management of non-native fish in China.

Because of its strong adsorption capacity and relatively low cost, biochar has become an important topic in wastewater treatment research worldwide. This review summarizes recent research on biochar, describes common preparation methods and modification strategies and their advantages and disadvantages, explains the mechanisms underlying its effects and its applications in aquaculture effluent treatment, and discusses barriers to wider development. It also proposes possible responses and considers future application prospects.

China ranks among the world's leading producers and exporters of farmed aquatic products. To ensure product quality and food safety, refined feeding practices and the development of precision-feeding equipment are increasingly important. The industry now emphasizes precision, digitalization, and intelligent operation of aquaculture equipment. This review considers progress in intelligent feeding systems based on four approaches: computer vision, acoustic monitoring, passive self-demand feeding, and decision-making models of growth and culture environments. It discusses development trends and the potential of digital and intelligent technologies to enable precise feeding management, improve farming efficiency, and promote further innovation in aquaculture equipment.

As aquaculture methods evolve, ecological technologies for water recirculation and reuse have been developed and applied. Constructed wetlands offer distinct advantages for recycling aquaculture wastewater. Through a review and analysis of relevant literature, this article summarizes the current status and challenges of using constructed wetlands to treat aquaculture wastewater and proposes technical strategies for upgrading wetland systems to overcome the limitations of conventional applications and improve water purification efficiency.

Real-time monitoring of abnormal fish behavior is important for improving aquaculture management, reducing disease risks, and optimizing feeding. To address blurred imagery, complex underwater backgrounds, diverse behavioral classes, and trade-offs between accuracy and computational efficiency, this study proposed YOLO11-AB, a robust detector based on an improved YOLO11 architecture. A multiscale convolution component (C3k2_PKI Module) was introduced into the backbone to improve perception of behavior features at different scales. During feature extraction, lightweight mixed local channel attention (MLCA) combined channel and spatial information. In the neck, a hypergraph-based cross-level representation network (HyperC2Net) and a mixed aggregation network (MANet) further strengthened recognition of abnormal behaviors in complex underwater scenes. Compared with conventional approaches, experimental results reported gains of 3.3 percentage points in precision, 5.9 percentage points in recall, and 4.4 percentage points in average precision. The approach may support early disease warning and management decisions in high-density industrial aquaculture.

Experience-based feeding methods in aquaculture often cannot predict feed demand over extended periods, contributing to feed waste, water pollution, and adverse effects on aquatic animal growth. This study investigated the main factors influencing feed quantity for catfish and selected water temperature, dissolved oxygen, ammonia nitrogen, average fish weight, total fish number, and weather conditions as model inputs. A multilayer perceptron (MLP) was trained on normalized data to estimate feeding quantities, and Bayesian optimization was used to tune its hyperparameters. Tests on data from different periods assessed model performance and generalization. In pond No. 11 during the peak feeding months of August and September, mean absolute percentage error remained below 4% and absolute error below 700 kg. The results suggest potential benefits for feed-use efficiency and aquaculture production.

To address systematic and accidental gaps in aquatic-environment data used for precision and intelligent aquaculture, this study proposed a dissolved-oxygen imputation method combining lagged causality analysis with an improved sequence-to-sequence imputation model (SSIM). Water-quality and meteorological observations were collected at a fixed sampling frequency. Based on Granger causality, a component-wise long short-term memory model (cLSTM) was used to analyze lagged relationships between environmental variables and dissolved oxygen, and variables with significant causal associations were selected as training inputs. An SSIM-based framework was then enhanced with a two-layer bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) and dropout regularization to represent complex temporal features. Reported mean absolute errors and root mean square errors were 0.04 and 0.05 for one-hour gaps, 0.16 and 0.17 for three-hour gaps, and 0.43 and 0.45 for five-hour gaps, respectively. The method provides an approach to water-quality data management in aquaculture.

Demand for aquatic products continues to grow with improvements in living standards. Fish farming is an important part of aquaculture, and increasing the production of cultured fish is a major challenge. Breeding has contributed substantially to production gains, but new technologies are needed to accelerate genetic improvement and meet the growing global demand for high-quality protein. Gene-editing tools, including zinc-finger nucleases (ZFNs), TALENs, and CRISPR/Cas9, are increasingly used for this purpose. CRISPR/Cas9 offers advantages in speed, cost, and editing precision and has therefore been adopted more widely in cultured fish. Researchers have improved desirable traits in more than 20 farmed fish varieties or species. This review summarizes the technology, its current applications in fish aquaculture, and future directions.

Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), also known as volatile fatty acids, are beneficial metabolites produced by the intestinal microbiota through dietary fiber fermentation. They can provide energy, support gastrointestinal function, regulate immune responses, and help maintain gut microbial balance. Research and applications of SCFAs in aquaculture remain relatively limited. This review discusses their use as effective feed additives and their potential effects on growth reduction, intestinal inflammation, and metabolic disorders associated with high-sugar and high-fat diets.

As aquaculture becomes more intensive, bacterial diseases of turbot have become increasingly important. This review summarizes the epidemiology of major bacterial diseases affecting turbot and examines current directions in disease prevention and control in aquaculture. It reviews advances in turbot disease-management technologies, including molecular breeding of new disease-resistant strains and biological control using bacteriophages. The review aims to provide a reference for healthy and environmentally sustainable fish farming.

To address the labor intensity and low efficiency of conventional marine aquaculture monitoring, this study proposed an Internet-of-Things-based environmental monitoring system that combines smart sensing, real-time processing, and remote control. The system enables continuous observation of culture conditions and precise remote adjustment of equipment. A three-month application case showed improved monitoring efficiency. Mean values from the monitoring system for temperature, pH, conductivity, turbidity, ammonia nitrogen, and dissolved oxygen were 28.36 °C, 7.82, 1,794.78 μS/cm, 0.25 NTU, 1.02 mg/L, and 7.81 mg/L, respectively. Corresponding manual-monitoring means were 28.35 °C, 7.82, 1,794.91 μS/cm, 0.25 NTU, 1.04 mg/L, and 7.77 mg/L. The close agreement suggests that the monitoring system can provide accurate measurements and support intelligent marine aquaculture.

Growing attention to marine aquaculture, driven by climate change and population growth, has accompanied increasing pressure on crowded coastal areas. Reconciling aquaculture with other maritime uses while protecting stakeholder interests is a central spatial-planning challenge. This review examines conflict coordination, carrying-capacity assessment, and spatial site selection. For conflict management, co-location and movement into deeper offshore waters have become major approaches, but implementation is limited by policy barriers and technical and economic feasibility. For capacity assessment, multidimensional frameworks covering physical, production, ecological, and social factors have been developed, yet a globally standardized approach is lacking and existing models struggle to capture complex stakeholder conflicts. For site selection, multicriteria decision analysis combined with geographic information systems is widely used, but static models have difficulty responding to changing marine environments. Future work should integrate artificial intelligence, big data, multiple data sources, adaptive dynamic models, and multipurpose maritime use to reconcile ecological protection and economic development.
